name: Best Pair
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$. Let $$$cnt_x$$$ be the number of elements from the array which are equal to $$$x$$$. Let's also define $$$f(x, y)$$$ as $$$(cnt_x + cnt_y) \cdot (x + y)$$$. Also you are given $$$m$$$ bad pairs $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$. Note that if $$$(x, y)$$$ is a bad pair, then $$$(y, x)$$$ is also bad. Your task is to find the maximum value of $$$f(u, v)$$$ over all pairs $$$(u, v)$$$, such that $$$u \neq v$$$, that this pair is not bad, and also that $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ each occur in the array $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that such a pair exists.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10\,000$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0 \le m \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the array and the number of bad pairs. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — elements of the array. The $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i \lt y_i \le 10^9$$$), which represent a bad pair. It is guaranteed that no bad pair occurs twice in the input. It is also guaranteed that $$$cnt_{x_i} \gt 0$$$ and $$$cnt_{y_i} \gt 0$$$. It is guaranteed that for each test case there is a pair of integers $$$(u, v)$$$, $$$u \ne v$$$, that is not bad, and such that both of these numbers occur in $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that the total sum of $$$n$$$ and the total sum of $$$m$$$ don't exceed $$$3 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case print a single integer — the answer to the problem.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1637E — Best Pair [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
